senses.definition_en: Used in emphatic negations, not even

examples.text: No tengo ni tiempo. ― I don't even have *time*.

examples.ref: Ni *tiempo* tengo. [Like in the example in the conjunction sense, the verb isn't negated.]

examples.text: Yo tiempo ni tengo. ― *I* don't even *have* time.

examples.english: The cool thing about getting a job is that I never know what's happening on GH [Gran Hermano = Big Brother] because I straight up don't even have time to watch it [Note that here ni is emphasizing tiempo and not tengo, but that doesn't sound natural in English]
examples.text: Lo piola de conseguir laburo es que nunca me entero [de] nada de gh por [que] directamente ni tiempo tengo para verlo
examples.translation: The cool thing about getting a job is that I never know what's happening on GH [Gran Hermano = Big Brother] because I straight up don't even have time to watch it [Note that here ni is emphasizing tiempo and not tengo, but that doesn't sound natural in English]

examples.english: Not even then, if your physical game needs a download it still doesn't matter, because they only sold you the license key in physical form.
examples.text: Ni así, si [tu] juego físico necesita una descarga también vale madres, porque solo te vendieron la key de la licencia en formato físico
examples.translation: Not even then, if your physical game needs a download it still doesn't matter, because they only sold you the license key in physical form.
